title.zh: 卷三七 補列傳第二九 魏收
title.raw: 卷三七 補列傳第二九 魏收 Volume 37 Biographies 29: Wei Shou

sentences.zh: 魏收，字伯起，小字佛助，鉅鹿下曲陽人也。

translations.literal: Wei Shou, styled Bowei, childhood name Fozhu, a man of Xiaquyang in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Wei Shou. Wei Shou, styled Bowei, childhood name Fozhu, was from Xiaquyang in Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖緝，祖韶。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Ji, grandfather Shao.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather was Shao.

sentences.zh: 父子建，字敬忠，贈儀同、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Zijian, styled Jingzhong, posthumously granted Pillar of the State and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei Zijian, styled Jingzhong, was posthumously made pillar of the state and governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 收年十五，頗已屬文。

translations.literal: Shou at age fifteen could already compose in writing.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Shou could already write compositions.

sentences.zh: 及隨父赴邊，好習騎射，欲以武藝自達。

translations.literal: When he followed his father to the frontier, he delighted in practicing mounted archery, wishing to distinguish himself through martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed his father to the frontier, he took to riding and archery, hoping to make his name by martial arts.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭伯調之曰：「魏郎弄戟多少？

translations.literal: Zheng Bo of Xingyang teased him, saying: "Young Wei, how much do you play with halberds?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bo of Xingyang jested, "Young Wei, how fond are you of waving halberds?

sentences.zh: 」收慚，遂折節讀書。

translations.literal: " Shou was ashamed and thereupon bent his will to study books.
translations.idiomatic: " Ashamed, Shou bent his will to books.

sentences.zh: 夏月坐板床，隨樹陰諷誦，積年，板床為之銳減，而精力不輟。

translations.literal: In summer months he sat on a plank bed, chanting along with the tree shade; year after year the plank bed was worn sharp by it, yet his energy did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he sat on a plank bed and chanted as he moved with the shade; over the years the bed wore thin at the edges, yet his vigor never flagged.

sentences.zh: 以文華顯。

translations.literal: He became renowned through literary brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: He won fame through literary brilliance.

sentences.zh: 初除太學博士。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was erudite of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱榮於河陰濫害朝士，收亦在圍中，以日晏獲免。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong wantonly killed court gentlemen at Heyin, Shou was also within the encirclement; because the day was late he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong massacred court officials at Heyin, Shou was caught in the roundup but was spared as dusk fell.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李神儁重收才學，奏授司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun, Minister of Personnel, valued Shou's talent and learning and memorialized to appoint him staff member of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun of the ministry of personnel prized Shou's talent and had him made staff secretary in the grand secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，除北主客郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he was made Northern Master of Guests Lang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an he was made northern master of guests lang.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝立，妙簡近侍，詔試收為《封禪書》，收下筆便就，不立稿草，文將千言，所改無幾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin was enthroned, he finely selected close attendants and ordered Shou tested by composing a "Fengshan Shu"; Shou put brush to paper and finished at once, setting down no draft; the text ran to nearly a thousand words, and few places were altered.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin took the throne, he culled his inner circle and ordered Shou to draft a Feng and Shan memorial; Shou wrote it at a stroke without notes, nearly a thousand words with scarcely a revision.

sentences.zh: 時黃門郎賈思同侍立，深奇之，白帝曰：「雖七步之才，無以過此。

translations.literal: At the time Yellow Gate Gentleman Jia Sitong stood in attendance, deeply marveling, and reported to the emperor: "Though one had talent for seven paces, one could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow gate gentleman Jia Sitong, standing by, was deeply struck and told the emperor, "Even the seven-pace talent could not outdo this.

sentences.zh: 」遷散騎侍郎，尋勑典起居注，並修國史，兼中書侍郎，時年二十六。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry; soon he was ordered to take charge of the Daily Record, and also to compile the national history, concurrently Secretariat Attendant; he was then twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made gentleman attendant of the scattered cavalry, soon ordered to keep the daily record and compile the national history, with concurrent secretariat attendant; he was twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，又詔收攝本職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, he again ordered Shou to take up his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign Shou was again ordered to resume his former posts.

sentences.zh: 文誥填積，事咸稱旨。

translations.literal: Literary edicts piled up; every matter met with approval.
translations.idiomatic: Drafts piled high and every piece pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎崔悛從齊神武入朝，熏灼於世，收初不詣門。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Juan followed Gao Huan of Qi into court and scorched the age; Shou at first did not visit his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow gate gentleman Cui Juan came to court with Gao Huan and blazed in influence, but Shou at first would not call on him.

sentences.zh: 悛為帝登阼赦，云「朕託體孝文」，收嗤其率直。

translations.literal: Juan drafted the enthronement amnesty for the emperor, saying "We have entrusted Our person to Emperor Xiaowen"; Shou mocked its bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: Juan wrote the enthronement amnesty with the phrase "Our body is entrusted to Emperor Xiaowen"; Shou laughed at its bluntness.

sentences.zh: 正員郎李慎以告之，悛深憤忌。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant Li Shen told him of it; Juan bore deep resentment and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Regular attendant Li Shen reported this, and Juan came to resent and fear him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時節閔帝殂，令收為詔。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Jiemin died; Shou was ordered to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin died, Shou was ordered to draft the edict of mourning.

sentences.zh: 悛乃宣言：收普泰世出入幃幄，一日造詔，優為詞旨，然則義旗之士盡為逆人；

translations.literal: Juan thereupon proclaimed: "In the Putai era Shou went in and out of curtains and canopies; in a single day he composed an edict, finely wrought in phrasing—then all the men of the righteous standard become rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Juan publicly declared, "In the Putai years Shou moved in the inner curtains; he composed an edict in a day with polished wording—by that logic every man who raised the righteous standard is a rebel;

sentences.zh: 又收父老，合解官歸侍，南臺將加彈劾，賴尚書辛雄為言於中尉綦儁，乃解。

translations.literal: further, Shou's father was aged; he ought to resign office and return to serve; the Southern Terrace was about to impeach him; he was spared only when Minister Xin Xiong spoke for him to commandant of the guard Qi Juan.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's father is old and ought to leave office to tend him; the southern terrace was set to impeach him until minister Xin Xiong pleaded with commandant Qi Juan, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 收有賤生弟仲同，先未齒錄，因此怖懼，上籍，遣還鄉扶侍。

translations.literal: Shou had a younger brother Zhongtong by a lesser mother, who had not been entered in the household register; in fear because of this he recorded him on the register and sent him home to support and serve.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had a younger half-brother Zhongtong, not yet on the family register; terrified by the scandal, he registered him and sent him home to care for their father.

sentences.zh: 孝武嘗大發士卒，狩於嵩少之南旬有六日。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu once mustered troops on a great scale and hunted south of Song and Shao for sixteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu once raised a great host and hunted south of Mount Song for sixteen days.

sentences.zh: 時天寒，朝野嗟怨。

translations.literal: The weather was cold; court and commonalty lamented in complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was bitter; court and people groaned in complaint.

sentences.zh: 帝與從官及諸妃主，奇伎異飾，多非禮度。

translations.literal: The emperor with his attendants and various consorts displayed strange arts and extraordinary ornaments, mostly outside ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, his attendants, and the palace women showed exotic tricks and outrageous dress, mostly beyond propriety.

sentences.zh: 收欲言則懼，欲默不能已，乃上《南狩賦》以諷焉，時年二十七，雖富言淫麗，而終歸雅正。

translations.literal: Shou wished to speak yet feared; wished to be silent yet could not stop, and so submitted "Nan Shou Fu" to admonish by indirection; he was then twenty-seven—though the words were lush and ornate, in the end they returned to elegance and rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Shou wished to remonstrate yet feared to; wished to hold silence yet could not, and submitted the "Fu on the Southern Hunt" as subtle counsel; he was twenty-seven—though the diction ran rich and ornate, the piece ended in sober propriety.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔報焉，甚見褒美。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote an edict in reply, greatly praising it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered in his own hand with high praise.

sentences.zh: 鄭伯謂曰：「卿不遇老夫，猶應逐兔。」

translations.literal: Zheng Bo said to him: "Had you not met this old fellow, you would still be chasing rabbits."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bo told him, "Had you not met me, you would still be chasing rabbits."

sentences.zh: 初，神武固讓天柱大將軍，魏帝勑收為詔，令遂所請。

translations.literal: At first Gao Huan firmly declined the post of Grand General of the Pillar of Heaven; the Wei emperor ordered Shou to draft the edict, letting him have what he requested.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan first firmly declined grand general of the pillar of heaven, the Wei emperor had Shou draft the edict granting his request.

sentences.zh: 欲加相國，問品秩，收以實對，帝遂止。

translations.literal: He wished to add the title Chancellor of State and asked about rank and grade; Shou answered according to fact, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne wished to make him chancellor of state and asked about rank and precedence, Shou answered plainly and the emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 收旣未測主相之意，以前事不安，求解，詔許焉。

translations.literal: Shou, having not yet gauged the intentions of sovereign and minister, was uneasy because of the earlier affair and sought release; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to read sovereign and minister, uneasy over past trouble, Shou asked to resign and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 久之，除帝兄子廣平王贊開府從事中郎，收不敢辭，乃為《庭竹賦》以致己意。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made Retainer of the Eastern Headquarters for the emperor's brother's son, Prince Zan of Guangping; Shou dared not decline and composed "Ting Zhu Fu" to convey his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was made eastern headquarters retainer to Prince Zan of Guangping, the emperor's brother's son; Shou dared not refuse and wrote the "Fu on Bamboo in the Court" to set out his feelings.

sentences.zh: 尋兼中書舍人，與濟陰溫子升、河間邢子才齊譽，世號三才。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Secretariat Drafter, and with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Shao of Hejian shared equal renown—the age called them the Three Talents.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was concurrent secretariat drafter, ranked with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Shao of Hejian; contemporaries called them the Three Talents.

sentences.zh: 時孝武猜忌神武，內有間隙，收遂以疾固辭而免。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowu was suspicious and wary of Gao Huan; within there were rifts; Shou thereupon pleaded illness and firmly declined, being relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu then suspected Gao Huan and rifts opened within; Shou pleaded illness and secured release.

sentences.zh: 其舅崔孝芬怪而問之，收曰：「懼有晉陽之甲。

translations.literal: His uncle Cui Xiaofen wondered and asked him; Shou said: "I fear there will be armor from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Cui Xiaofen, puzzled, asked why; Shou said, "I fear armor will march from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 」尋而神武南上，帝西入關。

translations.literal: " Soon after Gao Huan marched south and the emperor entered Guanxi to the west.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Gao Huan marched south while the emperor fled west into the passes.

sentences.zh: 收兼通直散騎常侍，副王昕使梁，昕風流文辯，收辭藻富逸，梁主及其群臣咸加敬異。

translations.literal: Shou was concurrently Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded and Upright Scattered Cavalry, assisting Wang Xin on a mission to Liang; Xin was elegant in manner and eloquent in letters, Shou rich and unbound in phrasing—the Liang ruler and all his ministers alike added respect and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Shou served as concurrent regular attendant for imperial missions and assisted Wang Xin on an embassy to Liang; Xin was elegant and quick in debate, Shou lush in ornament—the Liang ruler and his court all honored them.

sentences.zh: 先是南北初和，李諧、盧元明首通使命，二人才器，並為鄰國所重。

translations.literal: Earlier when north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming were first to carry missions; the talent and bearing of both were alike held in weight by the neighboring state.
translations.idiomatic: When north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming had led the embassies; both men's gifts were prized by the rival court.

sentences.zh: 至此，梁主稱曰：「盧、李命世，王、魏中興，未知後來復何如耳？

translations.literal: Coming to this, the Liang ruler said: "Lu and Li were men of an age; Wang and Wei revive the moment—who knows what those who come after will be like?
translations.idiomatic: Now the Liang ruler said, "Lu and Li belonged to a destined age; Wang and Wei revive the age—who knows what envoys will follow?

sentences.zh: 」收在館，遂賣吳婢入館，其部下有賣婢者，收亦喚取，遍行奸穢，梁朝館司皆為之獲罪。

translations.literal: " Shou in the lodge then sold Wu slave-girls to enter the lodge; among his subordinates were those who sold slave-girls, and Shou also summoned and took them, running riot in debauchery; Liang's hostel officers all were punished because of it.
translations.idiomatic: " In the embassy lodge Shou trafficked in Wu slave-girls; when his men did the same he joined them, debauching at will, and every Liang hostel officer involved was punished.

sentences.zh: 人稱其才而鄙其行。

translations.literal: People praised his talent yet despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Men praised his talent but scorned his morals.

sentences.zh: 在途作《聘遊賦》，辭甚美盛。

translations.literal: On the road he composed "Pin You Fu"; the diction was very beautiful and ample.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey he wrote the "Fu on the Embassy Journey," the diction splendid.

sentences.zh: 使還，尚書右僕射高隆之求南貨於昕、收，不能如志，遂諷御史中尉高仲密禁止昕、收於其臺，久之得釋。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi sought southern goods from Xin and Shou; they could not satisfy his wish, and he thereupon prompted Commandant of the Censors Gao Zhongmi to detain Xin and Shou at his bureau; after a long while they were released.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, vice director Gao Longzhi pressed Xin and Shou for southern luxuries; thwarted, he prompted censor commandant Gao Zhongmi to hold them at the censorate until they were freed long afterward.

sentences.zh: 及孫搴死，司馬子如薦收，召赴晉陽，以為中外府主簿。

translations.literal: When Sun Qian died, Sima Ziru recommended Shou; he was summoned to Jinyang and made Chief Clerk of the Inner and Outer Government Office.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Qian died, Sima Ziru recommended Shou; summoned to Jinyang, he was made chief clerk of the inner and outer government office.

sentences.zh: 以受旨乖忤，頻被嫌責，加以棰楚，久不得志。

translations.literal: For receiving orders in violation and opposition he was repeatedly blamed and reproved, and moreover beaten with the rod; for long he did not realize his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: His orders often missed the mark; he was blamed and beaten and for long found no favor.

sentences.zh: 會司馬子如奉使霸朝，收假其餘光。

translations.literal: It happened that Sima Ziru went on mission to the hegemonic court; Shou borrowed his surplus light.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ziru went on mission to the hegemonic court, Shou borrowed reflected glory.

sentences.zh: 子如因宴戲言於神武曰：「魏收天子中書郎，一國大才，願大王借以顏色。

translations.literal: Ziru at a banquet in jest said to Gao Huan: "Wei Shou was the Son of Heaven's Secretariat lang—a great talent of the state; I wish the Great King would lend him a favorable countenance.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Ziru jested to Gao Huan, "Wei Shou was the Son of Heaven's secretariat lang—a state talent; I ask the Great King to show him a kind face.

sentences.zh: 」由此轉府屬，然未甚優禮。

translations.literal: " From this he was transferred to a post in the government office, yet not greatly honored in courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: " By that he became a staff officer in the office, though not yet with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 收從叔季景，有才學，歷官著名，並在收前，然收常欺忽。

translations.literal: Shou's paternal uncle by the female line Ji Jing had talent and learning, his successive offices famed, all ahead of Shou—yet Shou often slighted and overlooked him.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Ji Jing was learned and had risen through famous posts ahead of Shou, yet Shou often slighted him.

sentences.zh: 季景、收初赴幷，頓丘李庶者，故大司農諧之子也，以華辯見稱，曾謂收曰：「霸朝便有二魏。

translations.literal: When Ji Jing and Shou first went to Bing, there was Li Shu of Dunqiu, son of the former Grand Minister of Agriculture Xie, famed for florid eloquence, who once told Shou: "The hegemonic court already has two Weis.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Jing and Shou first reached Bing, Li Shu of Dunqiu—son of the former grand minister of agriculture Xie, famed for florid debate—once told Shou, "The hegemonic court already has two Weis.

sentences.zh: 」收率爾曰：「以從叔見比，便是耶輸之比卿。

translations.literal: Shou bluntly said: "If you compare me to my uncle by the female line, that is like Yesu compared to you.
translations.idiomatic: Shou blurted, "If you liken me to my cousin, that's Yesu compared with you.

sentences.zh: 」耶輸者，故尚書令陳留公繼伯之子也，愚癡有名，好自入市肆，高價買物，商賈共所嗤玩。

translations.literal: Yesu was son of the former Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke Jibo of Chenliu, famous for dull-wittedness; he delighted in going himself into markets and shops, buying goods at high prices—the merchants together mocked and toyed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu was son of the former director of the masters of writing, Duke Jibo of Chenliu, notorious for stupidity; he loved to walk the markets and pay high prices, a jest to every trader.

sentences.zh: 收忽季景，故方之，不遜例多如此。

translations.literal: Shou slighted Ji Jing, and so compared him thus—his lack of deference was often like this.
translations.idiomatic: Shou despised Ji Jing and matched him so—his insolence was often of this sort.

sentences.zh: 收本以文才，必望穎脫見知，位旣不遂，求修國史。

translations.literal: Shou originally relied on literary talent and surely hoped to stand out and be known; office not being attained, he sought to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Counting on literary talent he had hoped to shine and be noticed; when rank failed him, he asked to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 崔進為言於文襄曰：「國史事重，公家父子霸王功業，皆須具載，非收不可。

translations.literal: Cui Jin spoke for him to Gao Cheng: "The matter of national history is weighty; your house's father and son hegemonic achievements all must be fully recorded—without Shou it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jin told Gao Cheng, "National history is grave; your house's hegemonic deeds, father and son, must all be set down—only Shou can do it.

sentences.zh: 」文襄啟收兼散騎常侍，修國史。

translations.literal: " Gao Cheng memorialized Shou as Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, compiling national history.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng had Shou made concurrent regular attendant of the scattered cavalry to compile the history.

sentences.zh: 武定二年，除正常侍，領兼中書侍郎，仍修史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding he was made Regular Attendant and concurrently led Secretariat Attendant, still compiling history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding he was made regular attendant, leading as concurrent secretariat attendant, still editing history.

sentences.zh: 魏帝宴百僚，問何故名人日，皆莫能知。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor feasted the hundred officials and asked why the day was called "Human Day"; none could know.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor feasted his officers and asked why the day was called Human Day; none could answer.

sentences.zh: 收對曰：「晉議郎董勛《答問禮俗》云：「正月一日為雞，二日為狗，三日為豬，四日為羊，五日為牛，六日為馬，七日為人。

translations.literal: Shou replied: "Jin Discussion Officer Dong Xun's 'Answers on Questions of Rites and Customs' says: "The first day of the first month is the cock, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the ox, the sixth the horse, the seventh is human.
translations.idiomatic: Shou answered, "Dong Xun's Answers on Rites and Customs says, "On the first day of the first month is the cock, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the ox, the sixth the horse, the seventh is mankind.

sentences.zh: 」時邢卲亦在側，甚恧焉。

translations.literal: " At the time Xing Shao was also at the side, deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Xing Shao, standing by, was deeply mortified.

sentences.zh: 自魏、梁和好，書下紙每卽：「想彼境內寧靜，此率土安和。

translations.literal: From the time Wei and Liang were at peace, whenever letters went down to paper it would at once say: "We trust that within your realm it is tranquil; within this realm all lands are at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Liang made peace, every letter opened, "We trust your realm is tranquil; here the empire is at peace.

sentences.zh: 」梁後使，其書乃云「彼」字，自稱猶著「此」，欲示無外之意。

translations.literal: " Later Liang envoys in their letters then used the word "that" realm, while for themselves still wrote "this"—wishing to show the meaning of having no outside.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Liang envoys wrote "that realm" yet still called their own "this," to show they admitted no outsider.

sentences.zh: 收定報書云：「想境內清晏，今萬國安和。

translations.literal: Shou fixed reply letters to say: "We trust within the realm it is clear and calm; now the ten thousand states are at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shou fixed replies to read, "We trust the realm is clear and calm; now the ten thousand states are at peace.

sentences.zh: 」梁人復書，依以為體。

translations.literal: " Liang men in replying letters took this as the model.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang envoys thereafter followed that form.

sentences.zh: 後神武入朝，靜帝授相國，固讓，令收為啟。

translations.literal: Later when Gao Huan entered court, Emperor Jing invested him as Chancellor of State; he firmly declined and ordered Shou to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao Huan came to court; Emperor Jing invested him chancellor of state; he declined, and Shou was ordered to draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 啟成呈上，文襄時侍側，神武指收曰：「此人當復為崔光。

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished and presented, Gao Cheng was then attending at the side; Gao Huan pointed at Shou and said: "This man ought again to be a Cui Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was done, Gao Cheng stood by; Gao Huan pointed at Shou and said, "This man will be another Cui Guang.

sentences.zh: 」四年，神武於西門豹祠宴集，謂司馬子如曰：「魏收為史官，書吾等善惡，聞北伐時，諸貴常餉史官飲食，司馬僕射頗曾餉不？

translations.literal: " In the fourth year Gao Huan feasted at the Shrine of Ximen Bao and said to Sima Ziru: "Wei Shou is history officer and writes our good and evil; I hear that during the northern campaign the great nobles often fed the history officers food and drink—did the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Sima ever feed them or not?
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth year Gao Huan feasted at the shrine of Ximen Bao and asked Sima Ziru, "Wei Shou as historiographer will write our good and evil—I hear nobles fed the historiographers on the northern campaign; did you, vice director Sima, ever feed them?

sentences.zh: 」因共大笑。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: They laughed together.

sentences.zh: 仍謂收曰：「卿勿見元康等在吾目下趨走，謂吾以為勤勞，我後世身名在卿手，勿謂我不知。

translations.literal: He then said to Shou: "Do not see Yuankang and others hurrying before my eyes and suppose I think it labor—my later-life person and name are in your hands; do not suppose I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: He told Shou, "Do not see Yuankang and the rest scurrying before me and think I mistake it for diligence—my name in later ages is in your hands; do not think I do not know."

sentences.zh: 」尋加兼著作郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made Concurrent Master of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made concurrent master of composition.

sentences.zh: 收昔在洛京，輕薄尤甚，人號云「魏收驚蛺蝶。

translations.literal: Shou long ago in Luoyang was exceedingly frivolous; people nicknamed him saying "Wei Shou startles the butterflies.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang Shou had been utterly rakish; men nicknamed him "Wei Shou, startler of butterflies."

sentences.zh: 」文襄曾遊東山，令給事黃門侍郎顥等宴。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng once toured Eastern Hill and ordered Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yuan and others to banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng once toured Eastern Hill and had attendant gentleman of the yellow gate Yuan and others hold a banquet.

sentences.zh: 文襄曰：「魏收恃才無宜適，須出其短。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng said: "Wei Shou relies on talent and is unfit for propriety—his shortcomings must be brought out.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "Wei Shou is insufferably proud—his faults must be aired.

sentences.zh: 」往復數番，收忽大唱曰：「楊遵彥理屈已倒。

translations.literal: Back and forth several rounds, Shou suddenly cried aloud: "Yang Zunyian's reasoning is bent and already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: After several rounds Shou suddenly shouted, "Yang Zunyian's argument is broken and down.

sentences.zh: 」愔從容曰：「我綽有餘暇，山立不動，若遇當塗，恐翩翩遂逝。

translations.literal: Yin at ease said: "I am broadly with surplus leisure, stand like a mountain unmoved; if I met the one on the road, I fear I would lightly flutter and pass away.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin calmly said, "I still have ample leisure and stand unmoved as a mountain; meet the one on the road and I fear I would flutter away.

sentences.zh: 」當塗者魏，翩翩者蛺蝶也。

translations.literal: "The one on the road" is Wei; "lightly flutter" is the butterfly.
translations.idiomatic: "The one on the road" meant Wei; "flutter away" meant butterflies.

sentences.zh: 文襄先知之，大笑稱善。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng had known it beforehand and laughed greatly, praising it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng had seen it coming and laughed with praise.

sentences.zh: 文襄又曰：「向語猶微，宜更指斥。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng also said: "The words just now are still subtle; you should further point and revile.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "That was still too mild—press harder.

sentences.zh: 」愔應聲曰：「魏收在幷作一篇詩，對衆讀訖，云：『打從叔季景出六百斛米，亦不辨此。

translations.literal: Yin answered at the sound: "Wei Shou in Bing composed a poem; when he had read it before the assembly he finished, saying: 'Beat out from my uncle Ji Jing six hundred hu of rice—you cannot tell this either.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin answered at once, "Wei Shou in Bing wrote a poem and read it before the crowd: 'Beat my cousin Ji Jing for six hundred hu of rice—you cannot tell this either.'

sentences.zh: 』遠近所知，非敢妄語。

translations.literal: This is known far and near—I do not dare speak falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone near and far knows it—I do not speak idle scandal.

sentences.zh: 」文襄喜曰：「我亦先聞。

translations.literal: " Gao Cheng delightedly said: "I too heard of it beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng said with delight, "I heard it too.

sentences.zh: 」衆人皆笑。

translations.literal: " The assembly all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: " The company laughed.

sentences.zh: 收雖自申雪，不復抗拒，終身病之。

translations.literal: Shou though he spoke to clear himself, no longer resisted, and for life was ill because of it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shou defended himself, he could not answer back and bore the wound for life.

sentences.zh: 侯景叛入梁，寇南境，文襄時在晉陽，令收為檄五十餘紙，不日而就。

translations.literal: Hou Jing rebelled and entered Liang, raiding the southern frontier; Gao Cheng was then in Jinyang and ordered Shou to draft more than fifty sheets of proclamation; in not a full day they were finished.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing defected to Liang and raided the south; Gao Cheng in Jinyang ordered more than fifty proclamations from Shou, finished within days.

sentences.zh: 又檄梁朝，令送侯景，初夜執筆，三更便成，文過七紙。

translations.literal: Again he proclaimed to the Liang court, ordering them to send Hou Jing; at the start of night he took up the brush, and by the third watch it was done—the text exceeded seven sheets.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted a summons to Liang to surrender Hou Jing—brush in hand at first night, done by the third watch, seven sheets and more.

sentences.zh: 文襄善之。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng was pleased with it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng was pleased.

sentences.zh: 魏帝曾季秋大射，普令賦詩，收詩末云：「尺書徵建鄴，折簡召長安。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor once in late autumn held the great archery rite, universally ordering poems composed; at the end of Shou's poem it said: "A letter a foot long summons Jiankang; a folded note calls Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor once held the autumn great archery and ordered poems; Shou's ended, "A foot-long letter summons Jiankang; a folded note calls Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 」文襄壯之，顧諸人曰：「在朝今有魏收，便是國之光采。

translations.literal: " Gao Cheng exalted it, turning to the crowd and saying: "In court today there is Wei Shou—he is the state's luster.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng exclaimed and told the assembly, "With Wei Shou in court today the state has its splendor.

sentences.zh: 雅俗文墨，通達縱橫，我亦使子才、子升時有所作，至於詞氣，並不及之。

translations.literal: Elegant and common, brush and ink, penetrating and running freely—I too have Zicai and Zisheng sometimes compose, but as for phrasing and tone, none reach him.
translations.idiomatic: High and low, ink and polish, all run through his hand—I set Xing Shao and Wen Zisheng to write at times, yet neither matches his tone.

sentences.zh: 吾或意有所懷，忘而不語，語而不盡，意有未及，收呈草皆以周悉，此亦難有。

translations.literal: I sometimes harbor a thought in mind, forget and do not speak, speak but do not exhaust it, or a thought has something not yet reached—when Shou presents drafts all are thorough; this too is hard to have.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes I harbor a thought, forget to speak it, speak but fall short—Shou's drafts fill every gap; that too is rare.

sentences.zh: 」又勑兼主客郎，接梁使謝珽、徐陵。

translations.literal: " He was further ordered concurrently Master of Guests Lang, receiving Liang envoys Xie Yan and Xu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made concurrent master of guests lang to receive Liang envoys Xie Yan and Xu Ling.

sentences.zh: 侯景旣陷梁，梁鄱陽王範時為合州刺史，文襄勑收以書喻之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing had already overthrown Liang, Prince Fan of Poyang of Liang was then Governor of Hezhou; Gao Cheng ordered Shou to instruct him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing overran Liang, Prince Fan of Poyang held Hezhou; Gao Cheng had Shou persuade him by letter.

sentences.zh: 範得書，仍率部伍西上，刺史崔聖念入據其城。

translations.literal: Fan received the letter and forthwith led his troops westward; Governor Cui Shengnian entered and seized his city.
translations.idiomatic: Fan received the letter and marched west with his men; governor Cui Shengnian took the city.

sentences.zh: 文襄謂收曰：「今定一州，卿有其力，猶恨『尺書徵建鄴』未效耳。」

translations.literal: Gao Cheng said to Shou: "Now in settling one province you had a share in the effort; I still regret that 'a letter a foot long summons Jiankang' has not yet taken effect."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng told Shou, "You helped secure a province today, yet I still regret that your line about summoning Jiankang has not come true."

sentences.zh: 二年，詔撰魏史。

translations.literal: In the second year an edict ordered him to compile the History of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the throne ordered him to compile the History of Wei.

sentences.zh: 四年，除魏尹，故優以祿力，專在史閣，不知郡事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Wei Intendant; therefore he was favored with salary and strength, devoted solely to the history hall, unaware of commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Wei intendant, favored with stipend so he could dwell in the history office and ignore commandery business.

sentences.zh: 初，帝令群臣各言爾志，收曰：「臣願得直筆東觀，早成《魏書》。

translations.literal: At first the emperor ordered the hundred ministers each to speak their intent; Shou said: "Your subject wishes to obtain the straight brush at Eastern Watch and soon complete the 'Book of Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor asked each minister his wish; Shou said, "Your servant seeks the straight brush at Eastern Watch and an early completion of the Book of Wei."

sentences.zh: 」故帝使收專其任。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor put Shou in sole charge of the task.
translations.idiomatic: " With that the emperor gave Shou exclusive responsibility for the work.

sentences.zh: 又詔平原王高隆之總監之，署名而已。

translations.literal: He also ordered Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi to supervise it in general, but Longzhi only appended his signature.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi to oversee the project, though Longzhi did no more than sign his name.

sentences.zh: 帝勑收曰：「好直筆，我終不作魏太武誅史官。

translations.literal: The emperor charged Shou, saying, "Keep a straight brush—I shall never act like Emperor Taiwu of Wei and kill the historians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged Shou, saying, "Write straight—I shall never do as Emperor Taiwu of Wei did and execute the historians.

sentences.zh: 」始魏初鄧彥海撰《代記》十餘卷，其後崔浩典史，遊雅、高允、程駿、李彪、崔光、李琰之徒世修其業。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Wei, Deng Yanhai compiled the Records of the Dynasty in more than ten scrolls; afterward Cui Hao took charge of the histories, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, Li Yan, and others in succession maintained the craft.
translations.idiomatic: " In early Wei, Deng Yanhai compiled the Records of the Dynasty in more than ten scrolls; later Cui Hao directed the histories, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, Li Yan, and others carried on the work generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 浩為編年體，彪始分作紀、表、志、傳，書猶未出。

translations.literal: Hao used the annalistic form; Biao first divided the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, but the book had still not appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wrote in annalistic form; Biao first divided the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, yet the book still had not been published.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，命邢巒追撰《孝文起居注》，書至太和十四年，又命崔鴻、王遵業補續焉。

translations.literal: In the Xuanwu era the court ordered Xing Luan to compile a follow-on Daily Records of Emperor Xiaowen; the text ran to the fourteenth year of Taihe, and Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were then ordered to continue it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu the court ordered Xing Luan to compile a Daily Records of Emperor Xiaowen; the text reached the fourteenth year of Taihe, and then Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were ordered to carry it on.

sentences.zh: 下訖孝明，事甚委悉。

translations.literal: It ran down to Emperor Xiaoming, and the events were set forth in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: It continued down to Emperor Xiaoming, with events recorded in exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 濟陰王暉業撰《辨宗室錄》三十卷。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiyin Huiye compiled the Record of Distinguishing the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiyin Huiye compiled the Record of Distinguishing the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 收於是與通直常侍房延佑、司空司馬辛元植、國子博士刁柔、裴昂之、尚書郎高孝幹專總斟酌，以成《魏書》。

translations.literal: Shou thereupon joined with Unimpeded Regular Attendant Fang Yanyou, Minister of Works Chief Clerk Xin Yuanzhi, National University Erudite Diao Rou, Pei Angzhi, and Masters of Writing Gentleman Gao Xiaogan in overall deliberation to complete the Book of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shou then joined Unimpeded regular attendant Fang Yanyou, minister of works chief clerk Xin Yuanzhi, national university erudites Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi, and masters of writing gentleman Gao Xiaogan in overall deliberation to finish the Book of Wei.

sentences.zh: 辨定名稱，隨條甄舉，又搜采亡遺，綴續後事，備一代史籍，表而上聞之。

translations.literal: He fixed names and titles, selected entries clause by clause, also searched out what was lost, stitched on later events, and completed the historical record of a whole dynasty, presenting it in memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed names and titles, chose entries clause by clause, recovered what had been lost, stitched on later events, and completed the historical record of a whole dynasty, then memorialized it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 勒成一代大典：凡十二紀，九十二列傳，合一百一十卷。

translations.literal: He brought to completion the great canon of an age: twelve annals and ninety-two biographical scrolls, one hundred and ten scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: He brought to completion the great canon of an age: twelve annals and ninety-two biographical scrolls, one hundred and ten scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 五年三月奏上之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year it was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year it was submitted.

sentences.zh: 秋，除梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn he was made governor of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed governor of Liang province.

sentences.zh: 收以志未成，奏請終業，許之。

translations.literal: Because the treatises were not yet finished, Shou memorialized asking to complete the work, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Because the treatises were still unfinished, Shou asked leave to complete them and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復奏十志：《天象》四卷，《地形》三卷，《律歷》二卷，《禮樂》四卷，《食貨》一卷，《刑罰》一卷，《靈徵》二卷，《官氏》二卷，《釋老》一卷，凡二十卷，續於紀傳，合一百三十卷，分為十二帙。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he again submitted the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena, four scrolls; Geography, three scrolls; Calendars and Pitchpipes, two scrolls; Rites and Music, four scrolls; Food and Goods, one scroll; Punishments, one scroll; Omens, two scrolls; Offices and Clans, two scrolls; Buddhism and Daoism, one scroll—twenty scrolls in all, continued after the annals and biographies, one hundred and thirty scrolls together, divided into twelve fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he submitted the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena (four scrolls), Geography (three), Calendars and Pitchpipes (two), Rites and Music (four), Food and Goods (one), Punishments (one), Omens (two), Offices and Clans (two), and Buddhism and Daoism (one)—twenty scrolls in all, appended to the annals and biographies for one hundred and thirty scrolls together, divided into twelve fascicles.

sentences.zh: 其史三十五例，二十五序，九十四論，前後二表一啟焉。

translations.literal: The history had thirty-five topical models, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and in all two tables and one memorial besides.
translations.idiomatic: The history had thirty-five topical models, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and besides two tables and one memorial.

sentences.zh: 所引史官，恐其淩逼，唯取學流先相依附者。

translations.literal: Of the historians he cited, fearing they might press upon him, he took only those of the scholarly current who had long relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the historians he enlisted, fearing they might crowd him, he took only scholars of his own circle who had long attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 房延佑、辛元植、眭仲讓雖夙涉朝位，並非史才。

translations.literal: Fang Yanyou, Xin Yuanzhi, and Sui Zhongrang, though long involved in court posts, were none of them talents for history.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanyou, Xin Yuanzhi, and Sui Zhongrang had long held court posts, yet none had a gift for history.

sentences.zh: 刁柔、裴昂之以儒業見知，全不堪編緝。

translations.literal: Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi were known for Confucian learning and were wholly unfit to compile and edit.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi were known for Confucian learning and were wholly unfit for compilation.

sentences.zh: 高孝幹以左道求進。

translations.literal: Gao Xiaogan sought advancement through heterodox arts.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiaogan sought advancement through heterodox arts.

sentences.zh: 修史諸人祖宗姻戚多被書錄，飾以美言。

translations.literal: The ancestors and affines of the men who revised the history were for the most part entered in the record and adorned with fine words.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors and affines of those who revised the history were for the most part written up and dressed in fine words.

sentences.zh: 收性頗急，不甚能平，夙有怨者，多沒其善。

translations.literal: Shou's nature was rather quick-tempered and not very even-handed; those who had long borne grudges against him had much of their good left out.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was quick-tempered and not very even-handed; those who had long borne him grudges found much of their merit omitted.

sentences.zh: 每言：「何物小子，敢共魏收作色！

translations.literal: He would often say, "What sort of stripling dares show color to Wei Shou!
translations.idiomatic: He would often say, "What sort of stripling dares stand up to Wei Shou!

sentences.zh: 舉之則使上天，按之當使入地。

translations.literal: Lift him and he goes to heaven; press him down and he goes into the earth."
translations.idiomatic: Lift him and he goes to heaven; press him down and he goes into the earth."

sentences.zh: 」初，收在神武時為太常少卿，修國史，得陽休之助，因謝休之曰：「無以謝德，當為卿作佳傳。

translations.literal: " When Shou was in Gao Huan's time Vice Director of the Imperial Clan and revised the national history, he received Yang Xiuzhi's help and therefore thanked Xiuzhi, saying, "I have no other way to repay your kindness than to write you a fine biography.
translations.idiomatic: " In Gao Huan's day, when Shou was vice director of the imperial clan and revised the national history, Yang Xiuzhi helped him; Shou thanked Xiuzhi, saying, "I have no other way to repay you than to write you a fine biography.

sentences.zh: 」休之父固，魏世為北平太守，以貪虐為中尉李平所彈獲罪，載在《魏起居註》。

translations.literal: " Xiuzhi's father Gu in Wei times had been governor of Beiping and, for greed and cruelty, was impeached and punished by Chief Commandant of Justice Li Ping, as recorded in the Wei Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiuzhi's father Gu had been governor of Beiping in Wei and, for greed and cruelty, was impeached and punished by chief commandant of justice Li Ping, as recorded in the Wei Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 收書云：「固為北平，甚有惠政，坐公事免官。

translations.literal: In Shou's book it says, "Gu governed Beiping with great benevolent rule and was removed from office for a public matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Shou's book it says, "Gu governed Beiping with great benevolent rule and was removed from office over a public matter.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「李平深相敬重。

translations.literal: " It also says, "Li Ping deeply respected him.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says, "Li Ping deeply respected him.

sentences.zh: 」尒朱榮於魏為賊，收以高氏出自尒朱，且納榮子金，故減其惡而增其善，論云：「若修德義之風，則韓、彭、伊、霍，夫何足數。」

translations.literal: " Erzhu Rong was a rebel against Wei; because the Gao clan sprang from the Erzhu line and Shou moreover accepted gold from Rong's son, he reduced Rong's evil and increased his good, writing in a disquisition, "If one cultivates the wind of virtue and righteousness, then Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang—what are they worth counting?"
translations.idiomatic: " Erzhu Rong was a rebel against Wei; because the Gao house sprang from the Erzhu line and Shou had also taken gold from Rong's son, he softened Rong's crimes and magnified his virtues, writing in a disquisition, "If one cultivates virtue and righteousness, then Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang—how are they worth counting?"

sentences.zh: 時論旣言收著史不平，文宣詔收於尚書省與諸家子孫共加論討，前後投訴百有餘人，云「遺其家世職位」，或云「其家不見記錄」，或云「妄有非毀」。

translations.literal: Public opinion had already said Shou's history was unfair; Emperor Wenxuan ordered Shou to the Masters of Writing to debate jointly with the descendants of the various families; before and after, more than a hundred people submitted complaints, saying "his family's hereditary posts were left out," or saying "his family does not appear in the record," or saying "there is groundless slander."
translations.idiomatic: Opinion already held that Shou's history was unfair; Emperor Wenxuan ordered Shou to the Masters of Writing to debate with the descendants of the various families; in all more than a hundred people complained that hereditary posts had been omitted, that their house was not recorded, or that they had been slandered without cause.

sentences.zh: 收皆隨狀答之。

translations.literal: " Shou answered each case as presented.
translations.idiomatic: Shou answered each complaint as it stood.

sentences.zh: 范陽盧斐父同附出族祖玄傳下，頓丘李庶家《傳》稱其本是梁國蒙人，斐、庶譏議云：「史書不直」。

translations.literal: Fanyang Lu Pei's father Tong was placed under his clan grandfather Xuan's biography as an attached entry; Dunqiu Li Shu's family biography said his origin was Meng in Liang; Pei and Shu criticized it, saying, "The history is not straight.
translations.idiomatic: Fanyang Lu Pei's father Tong was attached under his clan grandfather Xuan's biography; Dunqiu Li Shu's family biography said his line came from Meng in Liang; Pei and Shu protested that "the history is not straight.

sentences.zh: 收性急，不勝其憤，啟誣其欲加屠害。

translations.literal: " Shou's nature being quick, he could not bear his rage and memorialized that they wished to have him slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, quick-tempered, could not contain his anger and memorialized that they meant to have him killed.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，親自詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and personally interrogated and rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and personally interrogated and rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 斐曰：「臣父仕魏，位至儀同，功業顯著，名聞天下，與收無親，遂不立傳。

translations.literal: Pei said, "My father served Wei, rose to Pillar of State, his achievements were illustrious, his name known throughout the realm, and he had no kinship with Shou—yet no biography was made for him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei said, "My father served Wei, rose to pillar of state, his achievements were illustrious and his name known throughout the realm, and he was no kin of Shou—yet no biography was made for him.

sentences.zh: 博陵崔綽，位止本郡功曹，更無事跡，是收外親，乃為《傳》首。

translations.literal: Boling Cui Chuo held office only as merit officer of his home commandery and had no further deeds, yet as Shou's maternal kin he was made the lead entry of a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Boling Cui Chuo held office only as merit officer of his home commandery and had no further deeds, yet as Shou's maternal kin he led a biography.

sentences.zh: 」收曰：「綽雖無位，名義可嘉，所以合傳。

translations.literal: " Shou said, "Though Chuo had no office, his reputation and conduct were admirable, and therefore he deserved a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shou said, "Though Chuo had no office, his reputation and conduct were admirable, and therefore he deserved a biography.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿何由知其好人？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "How do you know he was a good man?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "How do you know he was a good man?

sentences.zh: 」收曰：「高允曾為綽贊，稱有道德。

translations.literal: " Shou said, "Gao Yun once wrote a eulogy for Chuo, praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Shou said, "Gao Yun once wrote a eulogy for Chuo praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「司空才士，為人作贊，正應稱揚。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "The Minister of Works is a man of talent; when he writes a eulogy for someone, of course he should praise him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The minister of works is a man of talent; when he writes a eulogy for someone, of course he praises him.

sentences.zh: 亦如卿為人作文章，道其好者豈能皆實？

translations.literal: It is just as when you write an essay for someone and speak of his good points—can they all be true?
translations.idiomatic: It is just as when you write for someone and speak of his virtues—can they all be true?

sentences.zh: 」收無以對，戰栗而已。

translations.literal: " Shou had nothing to answer and only trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had nothing to answer and only trembled.

sentences.zh: 但帝先重收才，不欲加罪。

translations.literal: But the emperor had long valued Shou's talent and did not wish to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor had long valued Shou's talent and did not wish to punish him.

sentences.zh: 時太原王松年亦謗史，及斐、庶並獲罪，各被鞭配甲坊，或因以致死，盧思道亦抵罪。

translations.literal: At the time Taiyuan Wang Songnian also slandered the history; Pei and Shu were both punished, each flogged and assigned to the armorers' ward, and some died from it; Lu Sidao was also punished.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Songnian of Taiyuan also attacked the history; Pei and Shu were both punished, flogged and assigned to the armorers' ward, and some died of it; Lu Sidao was punished as well.

sentences.zh: 然猶以群口沸騰，勑魏史且勿施行，令群官博議，聽有家事者入署，不實者陳牒。

translations.literal: Yet because mouths still seethed, he ordered that the Wei history for the time not be promulgated and commanded the officials to debate broadly, allowing those with family matters at stake to enter the office and submit memorials where things were untrue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because complaint still boiled over, he ordered the Wei history withheld for the time and commanded officials to debate broadly, allowing anyone with a family stake to enter the office and file memorials where facts were wrong.

sentences.zh: 於是衆口喧然，號為「穢史」，投牒者相次，收無以抗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon every mouth clamored and it was called the "Foul History"; memorials poured in one after another, and Shou could not withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon every tongue cried out and it was called the "Foul History"; memorials poured in one after another, and Shou could not withstand them.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射楊愔、右僕射高德正二人勢傾朝野，與收皆親，收遂為其家並作傳。

translations.literal: At the time Left Vice Director Yang Yin and Right Vice Director Gao Dezheng, the two men's power tilted the court and countryside; both were close to Shou, and Shou thereupon wrote biographies for both their houses.
translations.idiomatic: At the time left vice director Yang Yin and right vice director Gao Dezheng tilted court and countryside between them; both were close to Shou, and Shou wrote biographies for both families.

sentences.zh: 二人不欲言史不實，抑塞訴辭，終文宣世更不重論。

translations.literal: The two did not wish to say the history was untrue and suppressed the complaints; through the end of the Wenxuan era it was never debated again.
translations.idiomatic: The two would not admit the history was false and choked off the complaints; through the end of the Wenxuan reign it was never reopened.

sentences.zh: 又尚書陸操嘗謂愔曰：「魏收《魏書》可謂博物宏才，有大功於魏室。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing Lu Cao once said to Yin, "Wei Shou's Book of Wei may be called broad in learning and great in talent, with great merit to the house of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of writing Lu Cao once told Yin, "Wei Shou's Book of Wei is broad in learning and great in talent, with great merit to the Wei house.

sentences.zh: 」愔謂收曰：「此謂不刊之書，傳之萬古。

translations.literal: " Yin said to Shou, "This is a book that cannot be carved away—it will pass through ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Yin told Shou, "This is a book that cannot be carved away—it will pass through ten thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 但恨論及諸家枝葉親姻，過為繁碎，與舊史體例不同耳。

translations.literal: Only I regret that in discussing the branches, leaves, and affines of the various families it is too prolix and unlike the form of the old histories.
translations.idiomatic: Only I regret that in treating the branches, leaves, and affines of the various families it is too prolix and unlike the old histories in form.

sentences.zh: 」收曰：「往因中原喪亂，人士譜牒，遺逸略盡，是以具書其支流。

translations.literal: " Shou said, "Formerly, because the central plains fell into chaos, gentry genealogies were for the most part lost, and therefore I fully recorded their collateral lines.
translations.idiomatic: Shou said, "Formerly, when the central plains fell into chaos, gentry genealogies were largely lost, and therefore I fully recorded collateral lines.

sentences.zh: 望公觀過知仁，以免尤責。」

translations.literal: I hope you will see the fault and know the kindness, and spare me severe blame."
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will see the fault and know the kindness, and spare me severe blame."

sentences.zh: 八年夏，除太子少傅、監國史，復參議律令。

translations.literal: " In the summer of the eighth year he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and supervised the national history, again taking part in deliberating on statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: " In the summer of the eighth year he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent and supervised the national history, again joining deliberation on statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 三臺成，文宣曰：「臺成須有賦。

translations.literal: When the Three Terraces were completed, Wenxuan said, "When the terrace is completed there must be a fu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Terraces were completed, Emperor Wenxuan said, "When a terrace is finished there must be a rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 」愔先以告收，收上《皇居新殿臺賦》，其文甚壯麗。

translations.literal: " Yin had first told Shou; Shou submitted the "Rhapsody on the New Palace and Terraces of the Imperial Residence," and its text was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had warned Shou beforehand; Shou submitted the "Rhapsody on the New Palace and Terraces of the Imperial Residence," and its text was very grand.

sentences.zh: 時所作者，自邢卲已下咸不逮焉。

translations.literal: Of those who composed at the time, from Xing Shao downward none matched it.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who wrote at the time, from Xing Shao downward none matched it.

sentences.zh: 收上賦前數日乃告卲。

translations.literal: Several days before Shou submitted the fu he had only then told Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few days before submitting the rhapsody did Shou tell Shao.

sentences.zh: 卲後告人曰：「收甚惡人，不早言之。

translations.literal: Shao afterward told others, "Shou is a very hateful man—why did he not speak sooner?
translations.idiomatic: Shao later told others, "Shou is a hateful man—why did he not speak sooner?

sentences.zh: 」帝曾遊東山，勑收作詔，宣揚威德，譬喻關西，俄頃而訖，詞理宏壯。

translations.literal: " The emperor once toured East Mountain and ordered Shou to draft an edict proclaiming majesty and virtue and admonishing the lands west of the passes; in a moment it was finished, and its reasoning and diction were grand.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor once toured East Mountain and ordered Shou to draft an edict proclaiming majesty and virtue and admonishing the lands west of the passes; in a moment it was done, and its reasoning and diction were grand.

sentences.zh: 帝對百僚大嗟賞之。

translations.literal: Facing the hundred officials the emperor greatly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the hundred officials the emperor sighed in great admiration.

sentences.zh: 仍兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was then also made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then also made junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 收娶其舅女，崔昂之妹，產一女，無子。

translations.literal: Shou married his maternal uncle's daughter, the younger sister of Cui Angzhi, and she bore one daughter but no son.
translations.idiomatic: Shou married his maternal uncle's daughter, younger sister of Cui Angzhi; she bore one daughter but no son.

sentences.zh: 魏太常劉芳孫女，中書郎崔啟師女，夫家坐事，帝並賜收為妻，時人比之賈充置左右夫人。

translations.literal: The granddaughters of Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Fang and of Secretariat Gentleman Cui Qishi, whose husbands' families had been implicated in cases, the emperor bestowed on Shou as wives; men of the time compared it to Jia Chong's setting up a left and a right madam.
translations.idiomatic: The granddaughters of Wei grand master of ceremonies Liu Fang and of secretariat gentleman Cui Qishi, whose husbands' families had been implicated, the emperor bestowed on Shou as wives; men of the time compared it to Jia Chong keeping a left and a right madam.

sentences.zh: 然無子。

translations.literal: Yet there were still no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still had no sons.

sentences.zh: 後病甚，恐身後嫡媵不平，乃放二姬。

translations.literal: Later, when he fell gravely ill, fearing that after his death the principal wife and concubines would not be at peace, he released the two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he fell gravely ill, fearing strife between principal wife and concubines after his death, he released the two concubines.

sentences.zh: 及疾瘳追憶，作《懷離賦》以申意。

translations.literal: When the illness abated he recalled them with longing and wrote the "Rhapsody on Longing in Separation" to express his feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness abated he recalled them with longing and wrote the "Rhapsody on Longing in Separation" to express his feeling.

sentences.zh: 文宣每以酣宴之次，云：「太子性懦，宗社事重，終當傳位常山。

translations.literal: Wenxuan at every drunken feast would say, "The heir apparent is timid by nature; the altars of state are weighty affairs—ultimately the succession should pass to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan at every drunken feast would say, "The heir apparent is timid by nature; the altars of state are weighty—ultimately the succession should pass to Changshan.

sentences.zh: 」收謂楊愔曰：「古人云，太子國之根本，不可動搖。

translations.literal: " Shou said to Yang Yin, "The ancients said the heir apparent is the root of the state and must not be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shou told Yang Yin, "The ancients said the heir apparent is the root of the state and must not be shaken.

sentences.zh: 至尊三爵後，每言傳位常山，令臣下疑貳。

translations.literal: After the August One has taken three cups, he every time speaks of passing the succession to Changshan, making his ministers doubtful and divided.
translations.idiomatic: After His Majesty has taken three cups, he every time speaks of passing the succession to Changshan, making his ministers doubtful and divided.

sentences.zh: 若實，便須決行。

translations.literal: If it is real, it must be carried out decisively.
translations.idiomatic: If he means it, it must be carried out decisively.

sentences.zh: 此言若戲，魏收旣忝師傅，正當守之以死，但恐國家不安。

translations.literal: If these words are in jest, Wei Shou, having the shameful post of tutor, ought rightly to guard the heir to the death—only I fear the state will not be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If these words are in jest, Wei Shou, having the shameful post of tutor, ought to guard the heir to the death—only I fear the state will not be secure.

sentences.zh: 」愔以收言白於帝，自此便止。

translations.literal: " Yin reported Shou's words to the emperor, and from then on he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yin reported Shou's words to the emperor, and from then on he stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝數宴喜，收每預侍從。

translations.literal: The emperor often held feasts of pleasure, and Shou each time attended in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often held feasts of pleasure, and Shou each time attended.

sentences.zh: 皇太子之納鄭良娣也，有司備設牢饌，帝旣酣飲，起而自毀覆之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince took Zheng of the good secondary consortship, the offices prepared a full set of sacrificial meats; the emperor, already deep in drink, rose and himself overturned and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince took Zheng as good secondary consort, the offices prepared a full set of sacrificial meats; the emperor, already deep in drink, rose and overturned them himself.

sentences.zh: 仍詔收曰：「知我意不？

translations.literal: He then charged Shou, saying, "Do you know my intent?
translations.idiomatic: He then charged Shou, saying, "Do you know my intent?

sentences.zh: 」收曰：「臣愚謂長娣旣東宮之妾，理不須牢，仰惟聖懷，緣此毀去。

translations.literal: " Shou said, "This subject foolishly thinks that since the chief secondary consort is already a concubine of the Eastern Palace, by right she needs no full victims; looking up to consider Your Sagely intent, it was on this account that you destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shou said, "This subject foolishly thinks that since the chief secondary consort is already a concubine of the eastern palace, by right she needs no full victims; looking up to Your Sagely intent, it was on this account that you destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑，握收手曰：「卿知我意。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed greatly, grasped Shou's hand, and said, "You know my intent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed loudly, grasped Shou's hand, and said, "You know my intent.

sentences.zh: 」安德王延宗納趙郡李祖收女為妃，後帝幸李宅宴，而妃母宋氏薦二石榴於帝前。

translations.literal: " Prince Ande Yan Zong took as consort the daughter of Li Zu of Zhao commandery; later the emperor visited the Li house for a feast, and the consort's mother Song presented two pomegranates before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince Ande Yan Zong took as consort the daughter of Li Zu of Zhao commandery; later the emperor visited the Li house for a feast, and the consort's mother Song presented two pomegranates before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 問諸人莫知其意，帝投之。

translations.literal: He asked the company and none knew the meaning; the emperor tossed them aside.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the company and none knew the meaning; the emperor tossed them aside.

sentences.zh: 收曰：「石榴房中多子，王新婚，妃母欲子孫衆多。

translations.literal: Shou said, "The pomegranate has many seeds within— the prince is newly wed, and the consort's mother wishes many sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Shou said, "The pomegranate has many seeds within—the prince is newly wed, and the consort's mother wishes many sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 」帝大喜，詔收」卿還將來」，仍賜收美錦二疋。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased and charged Shou, "Bring them back," and at once bestowed on Shou two bolts of fine brocade.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly pleased and charged Shou, "Bring them back," and at once bestowed two bolts of fine brocade on Shou.

sentences.zh: 十年，除儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made Pillar of State of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made pillar of state of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 帝在宴席，口勑以為中書監，命中書郎李愔於樹下造詔。

translations.literal: At a banquet the emperor orally charged that he be made Director of the Secretariat and ordered Secretariat Gentleman Li Yin to draft the edict under a tree.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the emperor orally ordered him made director of the secretariat and commanded secretariat gentleman Li Yin to draft the edict under a tree.

sentences.zh: 愔以收一代盛才，難於率爾，久而未訖。

translations.literal: Yin, because Shou was a towering talent of an age, found it hard to compose offhand, and long went without finishing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, because Shou was a towering talent of an age, found it hard to compose offhand and long went without finishing.

sentences.zh: 比成，帝已醉醒，遂不重言，愔仍不奏，事竟寢。

translations.literal: By the time it was done the emperor had sobered from wine and did not speak of it again; Yin still did not submit it, and the matter in the end lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time it was done the emperor had sobered and did not speak of it again; Yin still did not submit it, and the matter lapsed.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩於晉陽，驛召收及中山太守陽休之參議吉凶之禮，並掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When the emperor died at Jinyang, couriers summoned Shou and Zhongshan governor Yang Xiuzhi to deliberate on auspicious and inauspicious rites, and both managed edicts and charges.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Jinyang, couriers summoned Shou and Zhongshan governor Yang Xiuzhi to deliberate on auspicious and inauspicious rites, and both managed edicts and charges.

sentences.zh: 仍除侍中，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was then made Palace Attendant and promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made palace attendant and promoted to director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 文宣諡及廟號、陵名，皆收議也。

translations.literal: Wenxuan's posthumous title, temple name, and tomb name were all Shou's deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan's posthumous title, temple name, and tomb name were all Shou's deliberations.

sentences.zh: 及孝昭居中宰事，命收禁中為諸詔文，積日不出。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao held affairs as regent in the center, he ordered Shou to remain within the palace to draft the various edicts and charges; for days he did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao held affairs as regent in the center, he ordered Shou to remain in the palace to draft the various edicts; for days he did not go out.

sentences.zh: 轉中書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇建元年，除兼侍中、右光祿大夫，仍儀同、監史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangjian he was made Concurrent Palace Attendant, Right Grand Master of the Palace, still Pillar of State, and supervisor of the histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian he was made concurrent palace attendant, right grand master of the palace, still pillar of state, and supervisor of the histories.

sentences.zh: 收先副王昕使梁，不相協睦。

translations.literal: Shou had earlier served as deputy to Wang Xin on an embassy to Liang and they did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had earlier served as deputy to Wang Xin on an embassy to Liang and they did not get along.

sentences.zh: 時昕弟晞親密。

translations.literal: At the time Xin's younger brother Xi was intimate with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xin's younger brother Xi was intimate with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 而孝昭別令陽休之兼中書，在晉陽典詔誥，收留在鄴。

translations.literal: But Emperor Xiaozhao separately ordered Yang Xiuzhi to hold the secretariat concurrently and at Jinyang manage edicts and charges, while Shou remained at Ye—this was Xi's doing, and Shou was greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: But Emperor Xiaozhao separately ordered Yang Xiuzhi to hold the secretariat concurrently and at Jinyang manage edicts, while Shou remained at Ye—this was Xi's doing, and Shou was greatly resentful.

sentences.zh: 蓋晞所為，收大不平，謂太子舍人盧詢祖曰：「若使卿作文誥，我亦不言。

translations.literal: He said to heir apparent attendant Lu Xunzu, "If you were made to compose edicts and charges, I too would say nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He told heir apparent attendant Lu Xunzu, "If you were made to compose edicts, I too would say nothing.

sentences.zh: 」又除祖珽為著作郎，欲以代收。

translations.literal: " He also made Zu Ting compiler in the Masters of Writing, intending that Ting replace Shou.
translations.idiomatic: " He also made Zu Ting compiler in the Masters of Writing, intending that Ting replace Shou.

sentences.zh: 司空主簿李翥，文詞士也，聞而告人曰：「詔誥悉歸陽子烈，著作復遣祖孝徵，文史頓失，恐魏公發背。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chief Clerk Li Zhu, a man of literary phrasing, heard it and told others, "Edicts and charges all go to Yang Zilie; compilation is again sent to Zu Xiaozheng—the literary and historical offices are suddenly lost; I fear the Duke of Wei will break out in a rash on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of works chief clerk Li Zhu, a man of letters, heard it and told others, "Edicts all go to Yang Zilie; compilation is again sent to Zu Xiaozheng—the literary offices are suddenly stripped; I fear the Duke of Wei will break out in a rash on his back.

sentences.zh: 」於時詔議二王三恪，收執王肅、杜預義，以元、司馬氏為二王，通曹備三恪。

translations.literal: " At the time an edict debated the Two Kings and Three Honored Guests; Shou held to the interpretations of Wang Su and Du Yu, taking the Yuan and the Sima as the Two Kings and Tongcao as supplying the Three Honored Guests.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time an edict debated the Two Kings and Three Honored Guests; Shou held to Wang Su and Du Yu, taking the Yuan and the Sima as the Two Kings and Tongcao as supplying the Three Honored Guests.

sentences.zh: 詔諸禮學之官，皆執鄭玄五代之議。

translations.literal: The edict ordered all officials of ritual learning to hold to Zheng Xuan's doctrine of five generations.
translations.idiomatic: The edict ordered all officials of ritual learning to hold to Zheng Xuan's doctrine of five generations.

sentences.zh: 孝昭後姓元，議恪不欲廣及，故議從收。

translations.literal: The empress of Xiaozhao was surnamed Yuan; in deliberating the protocol of respect they did not wish to extend it broadly, and so adopted Shou's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao's consort was of the Yuan clan; when the court debated the protocol of honoring former rulers, they did not wish to extend it broadly and followed Shou's view.

sentences.zh: 又除兼太子少傅，解侍中。

translations.literal: He was also made concurrent Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and relieved of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed concurrent junior tutor of the heir apparent and relieved of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝以魏史未行，詔收更加研審。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the Book of Wei had not yet been promulgated, ordered Shou to examine it further.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Book of Wei had not yet been issued, the emperor ordered Shou to review it again.

sentences.zh: 收奉詔，頗有改正。

translations.literal: Shou received the order and made many corrections.
translations.idiomatic: Shou obeyed and revised it extensively.

sentences.zh: 及詔行魏史，收以為直置秘閣，外人無由得見，於是命送一本付幷省，一本付鄴下，任人寫之。

translations.literal: When the order came to promulgate the Book of Wei, Shou held that placing it only in the Secret Archive left outsiders no means to see it; he therefore had one copy sent to the Bing office and one to Ye, and allowed anyone to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne ordered the Book of Wei circulated, Shou argued that locking it in the secret archive barred the public; he had one copy sent to the Bing secretariat and one to Ye and let anyone copy it.

sentences.zh: 大寧元年，加開府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daning he was given the distinction of opening an office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daning he was granted an open office.

sentences.zh: 河清二年，兼右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heqing he was made concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Heqing he was made concurrent right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時武成酣飲終日，朝事專委侍中高元海。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wucheng drank deep all day; court business was entrusted entirely to Palace Attendant Gao Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng then drank all day long, leaving court affairs entirely to palace attendant Gao Yuanhai.

sentences.zh: 元海凡庸，不堪大任，以收才名振俗，都官尚書畢義雲長於斷割，乃虛心倚仗。

translations.literal: Yuanhai was mediocre and unfit for a weighty post; because Shou's talent and fame stirred the age and Director of the Department of State Affairs Bi Yiyun excelled at decisive judgment, they relied on them with earnest trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai was commonplace and unfit for great responsibility; Shou's talent and fame shook the age, and Bi Yiyun as director of the department of state affairs excelled at cutting through cases—so the emperor leaned on them in earnest.

sentences.zh: 收畏避不能匡救，為議者所譏。

translations.literal: Shou shrank back and could not correct and save the situation; critics mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Shou shrank from remonstrance and could not set things right; critics jeered at him.

sentences.zh: 帝於華林別起玄洲苑，備山水臺觀之麗，詔於閣上畫收，其見重如此。

translations.literal: The emperor at Hualin Garden separately raised the Xuanyuan Park, furnished with the beauty of mountains, waters, terraces, and towers; he ordered Shou painted on a loft—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: At Hualin the emperor built the separate Xuanyuan Park, stocked with hills, water, terraces, and towers, and ordered Shou painted on a pavilion gallery—such was his favor.

sentences.zh: 始收比溫子升、邢卲稍為後進，卲旣被疏出，子升以罪幽死，收遂大被任用，獨步一時。

translations.literal: At first, compared with Wen Zisheng and Xing Shao, Shou was somewhat the later arrival; after Shao was dismissed and expelled and Zisheng died in prison for his crime, Shou was greatly employed and stood alone in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Shou had ranked after Wen Zisheng and Xing Shao; once Shao was driven out and Zisheng died in prison for his crimes, Shou rose to sole eminence.

sentences.zh: 議論更相訾毀，各有朋黨。

translations.literal: Critics tore one another down; each had his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Rivals slandered one another, each with his own clique.

sentences.zh: 收每議陋邢卲文。

translations.literal: Whenever Shou spoke he disparaged Xing Shao's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shou always spoke down Xing Shao's prose.

sentences.zh: 卲又云：「江南任昉，文體本疏，魏收非直模擬，亦大偷竊。

translations.literal: Shao also said: "In the south Ren Fang's literary style was by nature loose; Wei Shou did not merely imitate—he stole broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Shao also said, "South of the Yangtze, Ren Fang's style was loose by nature; Wei Shou did not just imitate him—he stole wholesale.

sentences.zh: 」收聞乃曰：「伊常於《沈約集》中作賊，何意道我偷任昉。

translations.literal: " When Shou heard it he said: "He often raids Shen Yue's Collected Works as a thief—what does he mean, saying I stole Ren Fang?
translations.idiomatic: " Hearing this, Shou said, "He is forever burgling the Collected Works of Shen Yue—why accuse me of stealing Ren Fang?

sentences.zh: 」任、沈俱有重名，邢、魏各有所好。

translations.literal: Ren and Shen both enjoyed great renown; Xing and Wei each favored one side.
translations.idiomatic: Ren and Shen both bore great names; Xing and Wei each took a side.

sentences.zh: 武平中，黃門郎顏之推以二公意問僕射祖珽，珽答曰：「見邢、魏之臧否，即是任、沈之優劣。

translations.literal: During Wuping, Yellow Gate Gentleman Yan Zhitui put the two lords' opinions to Vice Director Zu Ting; Ting replied: "To see whether Xing and Wei approve or condemn is to know the relative merits of Ren and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping, yellow gate gentleman Yan Zhitui asked vice director Zu Ting what the two grandees thought; Ting answered, "Judge Xing and Wei for praise or blame, and you know Ren and Shen's worth.

sentences.zh: 」收以溫子升全不作賦，邢雖有一兩首，又非所長，常云：「會須作賦，始成大才士。

translations.literal: Shou held that Wen Zisheng never wrote a fu at all, and though Xing had one or two pieces they were not his strength; he often said: "One must write fu before one becomes a true man of letters.
translations.idiomatic: Shou held that Wen Zisheng never wrote a fu at all, and though Xing had one or two, they were not his strength; he often said, "Only when you can write fu do you count as a great man of letters.

sentences.zh: 唯以章表碑誌自許，此外更同兒戲。

translations.literal: He claims only memorials, tables, stele, and epitaphs; everything else is child's play beside that.
translations.idiomatic: He rates himself only on memorials, tables, steles, and epitaphs; all else is child's play.

sentences.zh: 」自武定二年已後，國家大事詔命，軍國文詞，皆收所作。

translations.literal: From the second year of Wuding onward, the state's great affairs, edicts, and military documents were all Shou's work.
translations.idiomatic: From the second year of Wuding on, every great edict and military dispatch of state was Shou's.

sentences.zh: 每有警急，受詔立成，或時中使催促，收筆下有同宿構，敏速之工，邢、溫所不逮，其參議典禮，與邢相埒。

translations.literal: Whenever there was urgent alarm he received the order and finished on the spot; sometimes palace envoys pressed him—under his brush it was as if composed overnight. In swiftness of hand Xing and Wen could not match him; in deliberating ritual he was Xing's equal.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis struck he took orders and finished at once; sometimes palace envoys hurried him, yet his brush moved as if the piece had been drafted overnight—swiftness Xing and Wen could not match, while in ritual deliberation he stood even with Xing.

sentences.zh: 收以子侄少年，申以戒厲，著《枕中篇》，其詞曰：

translations.literal: Because Shou's sons and nephews were young he admonished them sternly and wrote the "Pillow Book"; its text runs:
translations.idiomatic: His sons and nephews still young, Shou warned them sternly and wrote the Pillow Book, which reads:

sentences.zh: 吾曾覽管子之書，其言曰：「任之重者莫如身，途之畏者莫如口，期之遠者莫如年。

translations.literal: I once read Master Guan's book, which says: "Of what is heavy, nothing weighs like the body; of roads to fear, none like the mouth; of deadlines far off, none like the years.
translations.idiomatic: I once read Master Guan's book, which says, "Of burdens none is heavier than the body; of roads none more fearful than the mouth; of distant deadlines none longer than the years.

sentences.zh: 以重任行畏途，至遠期，惟君子為能及矣。

translations.literal: To carry the heavy burden along the fearful road toward the distant deadline—only the gentleman can reach it.
translations.idiomatic: To bear that weight along that fearful road toward that far deadline—only a gentleman can arrive.

sentences.zh: 」追而味之，喟然長息。

translations.literal: Pondering it afterward, I sigh long.
translations.idiomatic: Turning it over afterward, I sigh at length.

sentences.zh: 若夫岳立為重，有潛戴而不傾；

translations.literal: As a peak stands upright in its mass, yet bears what is hidden beneath without toppling;
translations.idiomatic: A peak rises in its mass, yet bears what lies hidden beneath without toppling;

sentences.zh: 山藏稱固，亦趨負而弗停；

translations.literal: as mountains hoard their solidity, yet hurry forward under their load and do not stop;
translations.idiomatic: mountains hoard their solidity, yet press on under their burden without halt;

sentences.zh: 呂梁獨浚，能行歌而匪惕；

translations.literal: Liang alone dredged the torrent, yet could walk and sing without trembling;
translations.idiomatic: Liang of the ford dredged alone, yet walked and sang without fear;

sentences.zh: 焦原作險，或躋踵而不驚；

translations.literal: Jiao Yuan made the path perilous, yet some climbed its heel without alarm;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Yuan made the cliff road perilous, yet men climbed heel to heel unafraid;

sentences.zh: 九陔方集，故眇然而迅舉；

translations.literal: when the nine terraces gather, he rises swift in a blink;
translations.idiomatic: when the nine terraces gather, he lifts swift as a glance;

sentences.zh: 五紀當定，想窅乎而上征。

translations.literal: when the five eras are to be fixed, he seems to ascend remote above.
translations.idiomatic: when the five eras are to be fixed, he seems to climb far above.

sentences.zh: 茍任重也有度，則任之而愈固；

translations.literal: If bearing weight has its measure, then the more one bears the firmer it grows;
translations.idiomatic: If the burden has its measure, the more you bear the firmer you stand;

sentences.zh: 乘危也有術，蓋乘之而靡恤。

translations.literal: if crossing danger has its art, then one crosses and fears nothing.
translations.idiomatic: if crossing peril has its method, you cross and do not flinch.

sentences.zh: 彼期遠而能通，果應之而可必。

translations.literal: What is distant in deadline yet can be threaded through—when fruit answers, it may be relied on.
