translations.idiomatic: What is far in deadline yet can be threaded through—when the fruit answers, it is sure.

sentences.zh: 豈神理之獨爾，亦人事其如一。

translations.literal: Is it that divine principle alone is so? Human affairs are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Is it only divine principle that works so? Human affairs are alike.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 處天壤之間，勞死生之地，攻之以嗜欲，牽之以名利，粱肉不期而共臻，珠玉無足而俱致；

translations.literal: Between heaven and earth one toils in the ground of life and death; appetites assail one, fame and profit tug—fine food arrives unbidden, pearls and jade come though feet have not sought them;
translations.idiomatic: Between heaven and earth we toil on the field of life and death; appetites assault us, fame and gain pull—rich fare arrives unbidden, pearls and jade gather though we never went to fetch them;

sentences.zh: 於是乎驕奢仍作，危亡旋至。

translations.literal: then arrogance and extravagance arise in turn, and ruin follows at once.
translations.idiomatic: then pride and excess follow one another, and peril comes swift.

sentences.zh: 然則上知大賢，唯幾唯哲，或出或處，不常其節。

translations.literal: Thus the highest knower and greatest sage, wise in subtle signs and wise in judgment, now go forth, now withdraw, not holding to one constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the highest knower, the greatest sage—subtle in foresight, clear in judgment—now emerge, now withdraw, never fixed to one rule.

sentences.zh: 其舒也濟世成務，其卷也聲銷跡滅。

translations.literal: When they unfold they rescue the age and complete its tasks; when they roll up, their voices vanish and their tracks disappear.
translations.idiomatic: Unfolded, they save the age and finish its work; rolled up, voice fades and footprints vanish.

sentences.zh: 玉帛子女，椒蘭律呂，諂諛無所先；

translations.literal: Silks, jade, women, pepper and orchid, pitch pipes and notes—flattery finds no way ahead of them;
translations.idiomatic: Silks, gems, women, spice and song—flattery cannot get ahead of them;

sentences.zh: 稱肉度骨，膏唇挑舌，怨惡莫之前。

translations.literal: weighing flesh to measure bone, greasing lips and prying tongues—hatred and malice do not stand before them.
translations.idiomatic: weighing flesh, sizing bone, oiling lips, whetting tongues—malice cannot stand before them.

sentences.zh: 勳名共山河同久，志業與金石比堅。

translations.literal: Merit and name share the age of mountains and rivers; will and work match metal and stone in hardness.
translations.idiomatic: Fame and merit last with mountains and rivers; resolve and deed match metal and stone in hardness.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋厚棟不橈，遊刃砉然。

translations.literal: This is the thick beam that does not warp, the wandering blade that cuts clean.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the thick beam that does not warp, the blade that finds its gap.

sentences.zh: 逮於厥德不常，喪其金璞。

translations.literal: When virtue is not constant, the gold and jade within are lost.
translations.idiomatic: When virtue wavers, the gold and jade within are lost.

sentences.zh: 馳騖人世，鼓動流俗。

translations.literal: They gallop through the human world and stir the drifting vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: They race through the human world and stir the drifting crowd.

sentences.zh: 挾湯日而謂寒，包溪壑而未足。

translations.literal: They hug the sun's heat and call it cold, pack ravines and gullies and still find it not enough.
translations.idiomatic: They clutch the sun's warmth and call it cold, fill ravines and gullies and still are not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 源不清而流濁，表不端而影曲。

translations.literal: The source not clear and the stream runs muddy; the surface not straight and the shadow bends.
translations.idiomatic: Source unclear, stream muddied; face not square, shadow crooked.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 膠漆詎堅，寒暑甚促。

translations.literal: Glue and lacquer—how can they hold firm? Cold and heat press close.
translations.idiomatic: Glue and lacquer—how can they endure? Cold and heat crowd close.

sentences.zh: 反利而成害，化榮而就辱。

translations.literal: Profit turns to harm, glory turns to shame.
translations.idiomatic: Gain reverses into harm, splendor into shame.

sentences.zh: 欣戚更來，得喪仍續。

translations.literal: Joy and grief come in turn; getting and losing follow without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Joy and grief alternate; gain and loss follow without end.

sentences.zh: 至有身禦魑魅，魂沈狴獄。

translations.literal: Some guard the body yet are seized by demons; souls sink into the prison pit.
translations.idiomatic: Some guard the body yet are seized by demons; souls sink into the pit of law.

sentences.zh: 詎非足力不強，迷在當局。

translations.literal: Is it that strength of foot is not enough? They are lost because they stand in the game.
translations.idiomatic: Is it that the legs are weak? They are lost because they stand in the match.

sentences.zh: 孰可謂車戒前傾，人師先覺。

translations.literal: Who can say the cart warned of tipping forward, yet the man's teacher woke first?
translations.idiomatic: Who can say the cart warned of a forward fall while the driver's teacher woke first?

sentences.zh: 聞諸君子，雅道之士，遊遨經術，厭飫文史。

translations.literal: I have heard that gentlemen, men of the elegant Way, roam through the classics and feast on letters and history.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard of gentlemen, men of the elegant Way, who roam the classics and feast on letters and history.

sentences.zh: 筆有奇鋒，談有勝理。

translations.literal: The brush has a strange edge; discourse has winning reason.
translations.idiomatic: Their brush holds a keen edge; their talk holds winning reason.

sentences.zh: 孝悌之至，神明通矣。

translations.literal: When filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, the spirits connect.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety and brotherliness at their utmost—and the spirits respond.

sentences.zh: 審道而行，量路而止。

translations.literal: They weigh the Way and then walk; they measure the road and then stop.
translations.idiomatic: They weigh the Way, then walk; measure the road, then stop.

sentences.zh: 自我及物，先人後己。

translations.literal: From self to things, they put others before themselves.
translations.idiomatic: From self to things, they put others first.

sentences.zh: 情無繫於榮悴，心靡滯於慍喜。

translations.literal: Feeling is not tied to glory or decline; the heart does not stick in anger or joy.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling is not bound to rise or fall; the heart does not stick in anger or joy.

sentences.zh: 不養望於丘壑，不待價於城市。

translations.literal: They do not nurture hope in hill and ravine, nor wait for price in the market city.
translations.idiomatic: They do not nurse ambition in hill and dell, nor wait for a price in the market.

sentences.zh: 言行相顧，慎終猶始。

translations.literal: Word and act look back at each other; they are careful at the end as at the start.
translations.idiomatic: Word and deed watch each other; they guard the end as the beginning.

sentences.zh: 有一於斯，鬱為羽儀。

translations.literal: Where one of these is present, he stands as a feathered standard.
translations.idiomatic: Where one of these stands, he becomes a feathered standard.

sentences.zh: 恪居展事，知無不為。

translations.literal: Respectful in station, broad in service—what he knows, he does not leave undone.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful in his post, broad in his service—what he knows, he does.

sentences.zh: 或左或右，則髦士攸宜；

translations.literal: Whether left or right, the eminent man fits the place;
translations.idiomatic: Left or right, the eminent man suits the post;

sentences.zh: 無悔無吝，故高而不危。

translations.literal: without regret, without stinginess—thus high yet not in peril.
translations.idiomatic: without regret, without grudging—high yet not in peril.

sentences.zh: 異乎勇進忘退，茍得患失，射千金之產，邀萬鐘之秩，投烈風之門，趣炎火之室，載蹶而墜其貽宴，或蹲乃喪其貞吉。

translations.literal: Unlike the brave who advance and forget retreat, who clutch gain and fear loss, who stake a fortune of a thousand gold, who chase a salary of ten thousand bushels, who throw themselves at gates of violent wind and hurry into rooms of blazing fire—some trip and fall from their feast, others crouch and lose their firm good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Unlike the bold who advance and forget retreat, who clutch gain and dread loss, who stake a fortune in gold, who chase a stipend of ten thousand bushels, who hurl themselves through gates of violent wind into chambers of flame—some stumble from the feast they meant to keep, others crouch and forfeit their steady fortune.

sentences.zh: 可不畏歟！

translations.literal: Can one not fear?
translations.idiomatic: Can one not fear?

sentences.zh: 可不戒歟！

translations.literal: Can one not take warning?
translations.idiomatic: Can one not take warning?

sentences.zh: 門有倚禍，事不可不密；

translations.literal: At the gate disaster leans; affairs cannot but be kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate calamity waits; affairs cannot but be kept close.

sentences.zh: 墻有伏寇，言不可而失。

translations.literal: Behind the wall an ambush hides; words cannot be let slip.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the wall foes lie in wait; words cannot be let slip.

sentences.zh: 宜諦其言，宜端其行。

translations.literal: Examine your words; straighten your conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Scrutinize what you say; square what you do.

sentences.zh: 言之不善，行之不正，鬼執強梁，人囚徑廷。

translations.literal: Words not good, conduct not straight—the ghost seizes the bully, men bind him in the courtyard path.
translations.idiomatic: Words not good, conduct not straight—the ghost seizes the bully, men bind him in the open court.

sentences.zh: 幽奪其魄，明夭其命。

translations.literal: In darkness his soul is taken; in daylight his life is cut short.
translations.idiomatic: In darkness his soul is taken; in daylight his life is cut short.

sentences.zh: 不服非法，不行非道。

translations.literal: Do not submit to what is not law; do not walk what is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Do not bow to what is not law; do not walk what is not the Way.

sentences.zh: 公鼎為己信，私玉非身寶。

translations.literal: The public tripod is trust for the self; private jade is not treasure for the person.
translations.idiomatic: The public tripod is trust for oneself; private jade is no personal treasure.

sentences.zh: 過涅為紺，踰藍作青。

translations.literal: Pass the black dye and it turns indigo; cross the blue and it becomes green.
translations.idiomatic: Pass through the black dye and turn indigo; cross the blue and become green.

sentences.zh: 持繩視直，置水觀平。

translations.literal: Hold the cord and see what is straight; set the water and see what is level.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the cord and see what is straight; set the water and see what is level.

sentences.zh: 時然後取，未若無欲。

translations.literal: Take only when the time is right—not as good as having no desire.
translations.idiomatic: Take only when the time is right—better still to want nothing.

sentences.zh: 知止知足，庶免於辱。

translations.literal: Know where to stop, know what is enough, and you may escape disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Know where to stop and what is enough, and you may escape shame.

sentences.zh: 是以為必察其幾，舉必慎於微。

translations.literal: Therefore in acting one must examine the subtle; in lifting one must be careful at the small.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in acting one must read the subtle; in raising anything one must guard the small.

sentences.zh: 知幾慮微，斯亡則稀。

translations.literal: Knowing the subtle and thinking ahead, perishing then becomes rare.
translations.idiomatic: Read the subtle and think ahead, and ruin grows rare.

sentences.zh: 旣察且慎，福祿攸歸。

translations.literal: Having examined and being careful, fortune and rank return to you.
translations.idiomatic: Having examined and being careful, fortune and rank gather to you.

sentences.zh: 昔蘧瑗識四十九非，顏子幾三月不違。

translations.literal: In old times Qu Yuan recognized forty-nine faults; Yan Hui for almost three months did not stray.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Qu Yuan marked forty-nine faults; Yan Hui for nearly three months did not stray.

sentences.zh: 跬步無已，至於千里。

translations.literal: Half-steps without cease reach a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Half-steps without cease reach a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 覆一簣進，及於萬仞。

translations.literal: Overturn one basketful and advance, and you reach ten thousand ren.
translations.idiomatic: Overturn one basketful and advance, and you reach ten thousand ren.

sentences.zh: 故云行遠自邇，登高自卑，可大可久，與世推移。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: to go far, start near; to climb high, begin low—great and lasting, moving with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they say: go far from what is near; climb high from what is low—great, lasting, moving with the age.

sentences.zh: 月滿如規，後夜則虧。

translations.literal: The moon full as a compass—after that night it wanes.
translations.idiomatic: The moon full as a compass—after that night it wanes.

sentences.zh: 槿榮于枝，望暮而萎。

translations.literal: The hibiscus glorious on the branch—by evening it withers.
translations.idiomatic: The hibiscus blooms on the branch—by evening it withers.

sentences.zh: 夫奚益而非損，孰有損而不害？

translations.literal: What profit that is not loss? What loss that does not harm?
translations.idiomatic: What gain that is not loss? What loss that does not harm?

sentences.zh: 益不欲多，利不欲大。

translations.literal: Gain should not be many; profit should not be large.
translations.idiomatic: Gain should not be many; profit should not be large.

sentences.zh: 唯居德者畏其甚，體真者懼其大。

translations.literal: Only he who dwells in virtue fears its height; only he who embodies truth fears its breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Only he who dwells in virtue fears its height; only he who embodies truth fears its breadth.

sentences.zh: 道尊則群謗集，任重而衆怨會。

translations.literal: When the Way is honored, slanders gather; when the burden is heavy, many hatreds meet.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way is honored, slanders gather; when the burden is heavy, many hatreds meet.

sentences.zh: 其達也則尼父棲遑，其忠也而周公狼狽。

translations.literal: In his success Confucius was harried; in his loyalty the Duke of Zhou was hard pressed.
translations.idiomatic: In success Confucius was harried; in loyalty the Duke of Zhou was hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 無曰人之我狹，在我不可而覆。

translations.literal: Do not say others are narrow toward me—if I cannot bear it, I cannot cover it.
translations.idiomatic: Do not say others are narrow toward me—if I cannot bear it, I cannot cover it.

sentences.zh: 無曰人之我厚，在我不可而咎。

translations.literal: Do not say others are generous toward me—if I cannot bear it, I cannot blame them.
translations.idiomatic: Do not say others are generous toward me—if I cannot bear it, I cannot blame them.

sentences.zh: 如山之大，無不有也；

translations.literal: Like a mountain's mass, nothing is not held;
translations.idiomatic: Like a mountain's mass, nothing is not held;

sentences.zh: 如谷之虛，無不受也；

translations.literal: like the valley's hollow, nothing is not received;
translations.idiomatic: like the valley's hollow, nothing is not received;

sentences.zh: 能剛能柔，重可負也；

translations.literal: Able to be firm and to be yielding—then weight may be borne;
translations.idiomatic: Be firm when you must and yielding when you may, and heavy burdens will still be borne.

sentences.zh: 能信能順，險可走也；

translations.literal: Able to be trusting and to be compliant—then danger may be passed;
translations.idiomatic: Be steadfast in trust and supple in compliance, and even perilous paths may be walked.

sentences.zh: 能知能愚，期可久也。

translations.literal: Able to be wise and to be foolish—then one's span may be long.
translations.idiomatic: Know when to show wisdom and when to feign ignorance, and your days may endure.

sentences.zh: 周廟之人，三緘其口。

translations.literal: The men of the Zhou ancestral temple thrice sealed their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the Zhou ancestral temple sealed their lips three times over.

sentences.zh: 漏巵在前，欹器留後。

translations.literal: The leaky cup set before; the tilting vessel kept behind.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the leaky cup before your eyes and the tilting vessel at your back.

sentences.zh: 俾諸來裔，傳之坐右。

translations.literal: May all who come after receive it and pass it at the right hand.
translations.idiomatic: May posterity take it up and keep it at the right hand.

sentences.zh: 其後羣臣多言魏史不實，武成復勑更審，收又回換。

translations.literal: Afterward many ministers said the Wei History was untrue; Wucheng again ordered a further review, and Shou revised it once more.
translations.idiomatic: Later many officials declared the Book of Wei unreliable; Emperor Wucheng ordered another review, and Shou revised it again.

sentences.zh: 遂為盧同立傳，崔綽返更附出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote a biography for Lu Tong; Cui Chuo was moved back out and appended separately.
translations.idiomatic: He then composed a biography for Lu Tong and moved Cui Chuo's entry back out as a separate appendix.

sentences.zh: 楊愔家《傳》，本云「有魏以來一門而已」，至是改此八字；

translations.literal: In the Yang Yin family biography it had read, "Since Wei there has been only one house in the clan"—now he changed these eight characters;
translations.idiomatic: In the Yang Yin family biography the text had read, "Since Wei there has been only one house in the clan"—he now altered those eight characters;

sentences.zh: 又先云「弘農華陰人」，乃改「自云弘農」以配王慧龍自云太原人。

translations.literal: and where it had first said "a man of Hongnong, Huayin," he changed it to "claims to be of Hongnong," to match Wang Huilong's claim to be a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: and where it had first said "of Hongnong, Huayin," he changed it to "claims Hongnong," to match Wang Huilong's claim to be from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 此其失也。

translations.literal: These were his errors.
translations.idiomatic: These were his lapses.

sentences.zh: 尋除開府、中書監。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Secretariat Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed director of the palace secretariat and concurrently secretariat supervisor.

sentences.zh: 武成崩，未發喪。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died, mourning had not yet been proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng died, mourning had not yet been publicly announced.

sentences.zh: 在內諸公以後主即位有年，疑於赦令。

translations.literal: The ministers within the palace, because the Later Sovereign had already reigned for years, were uncertain about an amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: The inner ministers, since the Later Sovereign had already reigned for years, doubted whether an amnesty should be issued.

sentences.zh: 諸公引收訪焉，收固執宜有恩澤，乃從之。

translations.literal: The ministers brought Shou in for consultation; Shou firmly held that favor ought to be shown, and they followed him.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned Shou for counsel; Shou insisted that grace was due, and they followed his view.

sentences.zh: 掌詔誥，除尚書右僕射，總議監五禮事，位特進。

translations.literal: He directed edicts and rescripts, was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and in general supervised the Five Rites, with rank as Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: He directed edicts and rescripts, was made right vice director of the masters of writing, and oversaw the Five Rites in general, with the rank of special advance.

sentences.zh: 收奏請趙彥深、和士開、徐之才共監。

translations.literal: Shou memorialized asking Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, and Xu Zhicai to join him in supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Shou memorialized asking Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, and Xu Zhicai to serve as co-supervisors.

sentences.zh: 先以告士開，士開驚辭以不學。

translations.literal: He first told Shikai; Shikai, startled, declined on the ground that he was no scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He told Shikai first; Shikai, alarmed, declined on the ground that he was no scholar.

sentences.zh: 收曰：「天下事皆由王，五禮非王不決。

translations.literal: Shou said: "All affairs under Heaven are decided by Your Highness; the Five Rites cannot be settled without Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Shou said, "All affairs under Heaven are yours to decide; the Five Rites cannot be settled without you.

sentences.zh: 」士開謝而許之。

translations.literal: " Shikai thanked him and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Shikai thanked him and consented.

sentences.zh: 多引文士令執筆，儒者馬敬德、熊安生、權會實主之。

translations.literal: He brought in many men of letters to take up the brush; the Confucian scholars Ma Jingde, Xiong Ansheng, and Quan Hui in fact directed the work.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in many literary men to draft the text; the Confucian scholars Ma Jingde, Xiong Ansheng, and Quan Hui actually directed the work.

sentences.zh: 武平三年薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuping he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuping he died.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、尚書左僕射，諡文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of works and left vice director of the masters of writing, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 有集七十卷。

translations.literal: His collected works ran to seventy scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to seventy scrolls.

sentences.zh: 收碩學大才，然性褊，不能達命體道。

translations.literal: Shou was a great scholar of vast talent, yet by nature narrow-minded and unable to accept fate and embody the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was a great scholar of vast talent, yet by nature narrow and unable to accept fate or embody the Way.

sentences.zh: 見當途貴遊，每以色相悅。

translations.literal: When he met the powerful and noble of the day, he would always please them with a pleasant countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Before the powerful and noble of his day he always wore a pleasing countenance.

sentences.zh: 然提獎後輩，以名行為先，浮華輕險之徒，雖有才能，弗重也。

translations.literal: Yet he lifted up the younger generation and put reputation and conduct first; men flashy, frivolous, and rash—though they had ability, he did not esteem them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he championed younger men and put character before talent; flashy, frivolous, and reckless men he would not honor, however able they were.

sentences.zh: 初，河間邢子才及季景與收並以文章顯，世稱大邢小魏，言尤俊也。

translations.literal: At first Xing Zicai of Hejian and his brother Jijing were famed for letters together with Shou; the age called them Great Xing and Little Wei, saying Wei was the sharper.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Xing Zicai of Hejian and his brother Jijing had won fame for letters alongside Shou; the age called them Great Xing and Little Wei, saying Wei was the keener wit.

sentences.zh: 收少子才十歲，子才每曰：「佛助寮人之偉。

translations.literal: Shou was ten years younger than Zicai; Zicai would often say, "The Buddha helps the great man of the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was ten years younger than Zicai; Zicai would often say, "The Buddha aids the lodge's towering man."

sentences.zh: 」後收稍與子才爭名，文宣貶子才曰：「爾才不及魏收。

translations.literal: " Later Shou gradually vied with Zicai for renown; Wenyuan belittled Zicai, saying, "Your talent does not match Wei Shou's.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shou began to rival Zicai for renown; Wenyuan slighted Zicai, saying, "Your talent cannot match Wei Shou's."

sentences.zh: 」收益得志。

translations.literal: " Shou grew all the more elated.
translations.idiomatic: Shou grew all the more triumphant.

sentences.zh: 自序云：「先稱溫、邢，後曰邢、魏。

translations.literal: In his autobiography he wrote: "At first they spoke of Wen and Xing; later they said Xing and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In his autobiography he wrote, "At first they named Wen and Xing; later they said Xing and Wei."

sentences.zh: 」然收內陋邢，心不許也。

translations.literal: " Yet inwardly Shou looked down on Xing and would not concede it in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet inwardly he despised Xing and would not admit it.

sentences.zh: 收旣輕疾，好聲樂，善胡舞。

translations.literal: Once Shou fell ill, he loved music and was skilled at barbarian dance.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou fell ill he took to music and was skilled at barbarian dance.

sentences.zh: 文宣末，數於東山與諸優為獼猴與狗鬬，帝寵狎之。

translations.literal: At the end of Wenyuan's reign he several times on the Eastern Hill staged monkey-and-dog fights with performers; the emperor doted on him familiarly.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wenyuan's reign he several times on the Eastern Hill staged monkey-and-dog fights with performers; the emperor treated him with familiar affection.

sentences.zh: 收外兄博陵崔巖嘗以雙聲嘲收曰：「愚魏衰收。

translations.literal: His mother's sister's son Cui Yan of Boling once mocked him with shuang-sheng wordplay, saying: "Fool-Wei, fade-Shou.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's sister's son Cui Yan of Boling once mocked him with paired-alliteration verse, saying, "Fool-Wei, fade-Shou."

sentences.zh: 」收答曰：「顏巖腥瘦，是誰所生，羊頤狗頰，頭團鼻平，飯房苓籠，著孔嘲玎。

translations.literal: " Shou replied: "Yan-face, rank-lean—whose whelp are you? Sheep-jaw, dog-cheek; knob-head, flat-nose. Meal-barracks, tuckah-cage—stop-hole, sting-mock.
translations.idiomatic: Shou replied, "Yan-face, rank-lean—whose whelp are you? Sheep-jaw, dog-cheek; knob-head, flat-nose. Meal-barracks, tuckah-cage—stop-hole, sting-mock!"

sentences.zh: 」其辯捷不拘若是。

translations.literal: " His nimble retort was unrestrained in just this way.
translations.idiomatic: His repartee was as nimble and unrestrained as that.

sentences.zh: 旣緣史筆，多憾於人。

translations.literal: Once he held the brush of history, he earned much resentment from others.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the historian's brush, he earned much resentment.

sentences.zh: 齊亡之歲，收冢被發，棄其骨于外。

translations.literal: In the year Qi fell, Shou's tomb was opened and his bones cast out.
translations.idiomatic: In the year Qi fell, Shou's tomb was opened and his bones thrown out.

sentences.zh: 先養弟子仁表為嗣，位至尚書膳部郎中。

translations.literal: He had earlier adopted his nephew Renbiao as heir; Renbiao rose to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Board of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier adopted his nephew Renbiao as heir; Renbiao rose to gentleman of the masters of writing in the board of provisions.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒於溫縣令。

translations.literal: In the Sui Kaihuang era he died in office as magistrate of Wen county.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui Kaihuang era he died in office as magistrate of Wen county.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
